label: context.reference
text:
How to author another run in Octopus: its record is ordinary JSON, and its creation effects are checked file tools followed by artifact movement. A model-visible composition affordance may prepare those same effects when its current descriptor and grant expose it; follow its advertised schema and evidence contract. The manual file path below uses the same primitives. It begins receiving work only when an artifact crosses an exact interface folder authored on one of its active checkpoints.

1. RUN RECORD. Obtain the current run schema from a readable bound authoring artifact (artifact-home-task-authoring includes run_record_schema.document) or an explicitly granted schema path. A source path such as schemas/run_record.schema.json is provenance, not permission to read the provider workspace. If no schema is readable, report that exact missing context contract before authoring a record. The file stem must equal id. A current record contains {id, ee, worker, trace, status, interface_state, checkpoints, active_checkpoints}; run trace is a non-empty authored lineage string. Every checkpoint contains its own non-empty trace plus id, run, epoch, optional interface_binding, outbound_interface_bindings, artifact_bindings, and required_verified_artifacts. Each interface binding is an object {interface, config:{artifact_policy}}. artifact_policy is explicit: either {mode:"all"} or {mode:"allow", names:[...], namespaces:[...]}; it is never omitted and a bare interface string is invalid. Artifact bindings are {id} or {id, access}; they never contain a content hash. FormationPin and the formed grant are runtime-attested movement metadata, never authored run fields. The file tool writes bytes; runtime re-reads the completed JSON fail-closed.

2. IDENTITY. An interface's only routing and policy identity is its registry/interface folder. There are no binding names, session lanes, labels-as-routes, family grants, or second interface ids. Reusing another interface's code is an implementation import only. A run that needs an isolated edge authors a new exact interface folder and every policy surface that permits it names that exact id.

3. GRANT. The run's grant is worker-interface ceiling ∩ the EE chain where the run lives ∩ the run's authored exact bindings. The initiator's grant does not clamp it. Choose an existing EE whose chain permits the worker pin and each required exact interface; writing extra bindings cannot widen the formed grant.

4. MODEL-POWERED RUN. The run names an exact system_worker_* pin and an exact provider interface through its checkpoints. A task-scoped concrete provider folder may reuse provider code, but its descriptor stays run-agnostic: run_authoring_profile names only the exact authoring tool/labels/timeout. Run, worker, checkpoint, EE, epoch, and provider coordinates come from attested invocation metadata plus the live run record; never write reverse run/worker ownership into provider config. Provider model and reasoning variables are interface policy/config, not interface identity and not runtime selectors. Interface-private auth/state stays behind that exact provider boundary.

5. CHECKPOINT DIRECTIONS. The input checkpoint binds the exact source interface that receives the task and routes outbound to the provider. A provider-output checkpoint binds the provider and routes each artifact to its authored receiver. If provider code must advance the run, give it an exact file-tool door through separate authoring-call and authoring-result checkpoints; this is an ordinary gated file effect, not a runtime authoring API. Other tool doors likewise use separate provider-output and tool-result edges.

6. ROLE AND CONTEXT. Bind role, grounding, documentation, and prior-result artifacts as ordinary {id} artifact_bindings on every checkpoint that must see them. Artifact refs are content-addressed evidence; the provider/interface materializes them. A tool-less model run simply has no model-visible tool-door binding. Provider-native context compaction replaces only that provider interface's private model history and continues the same turn in the same run; Octopus records the compaction as evidence and never migrates the task. A future separate compactor run may return an explicit summary artifact to the original run, but it does not replace that run.

7. RETURN AND JOIN. Return work by routing a provider output artifact through an authored exact outbound interface. If a receiving checkpoint needs proof, it authors required_verified_artifacts; runtime records the mark only after the referenced verifier passes. An unmet requirement is data, not a blocked process, lease, or deadlock.

8. artifact.send. Use artifact.send only when the model must choose an address instead of following an already-authored outbound edge. The target exact interface must already be present in the active authored binding surface and in the formed grant, and the artifact must satisfy every matching binding's artifact policy. The result is admitted {seq} or a typed refusal, never the receiver's reply. An admitted outbound with no live reader is still success; the interface catches up from its own cursor.
description: Current run JSON shape, exact checkpoint directions, role bindings and artifact-send admission for authoring another run.
